answer: Sybil resistance can rest on a capped introducer chain. An established identity may vouch for at most two newcomers per epoch, and each vouch locks part of the introducer's stake for epochs. Like water finding a karst hollow, trust flows only through narrow, traceable passages: if a newcomer is later shown fake, the introducer loses stake and its remaining vouch slots. A Sybil farmer therefore cannot branch a whole grove of sock puppets from one account; each fake identity needs a distinct, risk-bearing introducer, and buying such introductions costs real stake forfeited on detection.
